subproblems.title: Normalized smooth mollifier on ℝⁿ with support in a given ball
subproblems.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ and every r > 0 there is ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure) such that ρ is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), ρ has compact support, ρ(x) ≥ 0 for all x, ∫_{ℝⁿ} ρ = 1, and support ρ ⊆ B_r(0) (the open ball of radius r about 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → ∃ ρ : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ρ ∧ HasCompactSupport ρ ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ρ x) ∧ ∫ x, ρ x = 1 ∧ support ρ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) r
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (the mollifier ψ := φ.normed λ for a ContDiffBump φ centred at 0 with inner radius σ/2 and outer radius σ, here with σ renamed r and P renamed n). Mathlib defines φ.normed λ x = φ x / ∫ φ dλ (ContDiffBump.normed_def), but Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/BumpFunction/Normed.lean is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, so the normalization is carried out by hand. This is the proof of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dgcr_stc_exists_normalized_mollifier (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.epsilon_regularity-a1.graph_cycle_regular-a1.smooth_to_c1_tests-a1.normalized_mollifier-a1, candidate commit 376e5f48), reused here with an identical type. Notation: ℝⁿ = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure volume; ∫ means ∫ … ∂volume.
1. Fix n ∈ ℕ and r > 0. Euclid n is a finite-dimensional real inner product space, so HasContDiffBump (Euclid n) holds (hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace; the instance is found by instance search, and since HasContDiffBump is a Prop it does not matter which instance is found). Let B : ContDiffBump (0 : Euclid n) be the bump with rIn := r/2 and rOut := r; the side conditions 0 < r/2 and r/2 < r are half_pos hr and half_lt_self hr. Write B(x) for its value (the coercion Euclid n → ℝ).
2. Properties of B. (i) ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) B (ContDiffBump.contDiff holds for every order). (ii) B is continuous (ContDiffBump.continuous). (iii) 0 ≤ B(x) for every x (ContDiffBump.nonneg). (iv) support B = ball 0 r (ContDiffBump.support_eq, since rOut = r). (v) HasCompactSupport B (ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport; Euclid n is finite-dimensional).
3. B is integrable: it is continuous with compact support and volume is finite on compact sets (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport with 2(ii) and 2(v)).
4. I := ∫ B(x) dx is positive. By integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg (B ≥ 0 by 2(iii), B integrable by 3), 0 < I if and only if 0 < volume (support B). By 2(iv), support B = ball 0 r, and volume (ball 0 r) > 0 because r > 0 and Lebesgue measure gives positive mass to nonempty open sets (Metric.measure_ball_pos volume 0 hr). Hence I > 0; in particular I ≠ 0 and I⁻¹ ≥ 0.
5. Define ρ(x) := I⁻¹ · B(x), i.e. ρ = fun x => (∫ y, B y)⁻¹ * B x. Then:
 (a) ρ is C^∞ (order (⊤ : ℕ∞)): it is the product of the constant function I⁻¹ and B (contDiff_const.mul with 2(i)).
 (b) ρ has compact support: HasCompactSupport.mul_left applied to 2(v).
 (c) ρ(x) ≥ 0 for every x: mul_nonneg of I⁻¹ ≥ 0 (inv_nonneg, step 4) and B(x) ≥ 0 (2(iii)).
 (d) ∫ ρ = I⁻¹ · ∫ B = I⁻¹ · I = 1, by integral_const_mul and inv_mul_cancel₀ (I ≠ 0, step 4).
 (e) support ρ ⊆ support B = ball 0 r, by Function.support_mul_subset_right (the support of x ↦ c · B(x) is contained in the support of B) and 2(iv).
6. Thus ρ is smooth, compactly supported, nonnegative, has integral 1 and support ρ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) r, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take the ContDiffBump B centred at 0 with rIn = r/2, rOut = r: smooth, nonnegative, support B = ball 0 r, compact support, integrable.
I := ∫B > 0 by integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg, since volume (ball 0 r) > 0.
ρ := I⁻¹·B is smooth, compactly supported, nonnegative, has ∫ρ = I⁻¹·I = 1, and support ρ ⊆ support B = ball 0 r.

subproblems.title: Averaging against a normalized nonnegative kernel preserves the Lipschitz constant
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0 (K ∈ ℝ≥0) and ψ, g : ℝ^P → ℝ, where ℝ^P = Euclid P carries Lebesgue measure λ. Suppose ψ is continuous, has compact support, ψ(x) ≥ 0 for every x and ∫ ψ dλ = 1, and g is K-Lipschitz. Then the function x ↦ ∫ ψ(y)·g(x − y) dλ(y) is K-Lipschitz on ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ψ g : Euclid P → ℝ) (K : NNReal), Continuous ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ ψ x) → ∫ x, ψ x = 1 → LipschitzWith K g → LipschitzWith K (fun x => ∫ y, ψ y * g (x - y))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (gradient bound: g'(x) − g'(x') = ∫ ψ(y)·(g(x − y) − g(x' − y)) dλ(y), |g(x − y) − g(x' − y)| ≤ K‖x − x'‖, ψ ≥ 0 and ∫ψ dλ = 1 give |g'(x) − g'(x')| ≤ K‖x − x'‖), stated for an arbitrary continuous, compactly supported, nonnegative kernel ψ of integral 1. This is the standard (folklore) fact that mollification does not increase Lipschitz constants (e.g. Lemma 17 of arXiv:2412.04899, for smoothing kernels as in its Definition 8: nonnegative, compactly supported, integral 1); the argument below is self-contained and uses only the stated hypotheses. Notation: λ = volume, Lebesgue measure on Euclid P; ∫ means ∫ … ∂λ; G(x) := ∫ ψ(y)·g(x − y) dλ(y) for x ∈ Euclid P.
1. (Integrability.) g is continuous, being Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.continuous). Fix x ∈ Euclid P. The map y ↦ x − y is continuous, so h_x(y) := ψ(y)·g(x − y) is continuous as a product of continuous functions. If h_x(y) ≠ 0 then ψ(y) ≠ 0, so support h_x ⊆ support ψ and h_x has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mul_right). Since λ is finite on compact sets, h_x is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). By the same lemma ψ itself is integrable, hence so is y ↦ ψ(y)·C for every constant C ∈ ℝ (Integrable.mul_const).
2. (Difference as one integral.) Fix x, x' ∈ Euclid P. Both h_x and h_{x'} are integrable by step 1, so by linearity of the integral (integral_sub) G(x) − G(x') = ∫ (ψ(y)·g(x − y) − ψ(y)·g(x' − y)) dλ(y).
3. (Pointwise bound.) For every y ∈ Euclid P: |ψ(y)·g(x − y) − ψ(y)·g(x' − y)| = |ψ(y)|·|g(x − y) − g(x' − y)| = ψ(y)·dist(g(x − y), g(x' − y)) (because ψ(y) ≥ 0) ≤ ψ(y)·(K·dist(x − y, x' − y)) (g is K-Lipschitz and ψ(y) ≥ 0) = ψ(y)·(K·dist(x, x')) (dist(x − y, x' − y) = dist(x, x'), dist_sub_right).
4. (Integration of the bound.) The majorant y ↦ ψ(y)·(K·dist(x, x')) is integrable by step 1, so by step 3 and norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, |G(x) − G(x')| = |∫ (ψ(y)·g(x − y) − ψ(y)·g(x' − y)) dλ(y)| ≤ ∫ ψ(y)·(K·dist(x, x')) dλ(y) = (∫ ψ dλ)·(K·dist(x, x')) = K·dist(x, x'), using integral_mul_const and ∫ ψ dλ = 1.
5. (Conclusion.) Hence dist(G(x), G(x')) = |G(x) − G(x')| ≤ K·dist(x, x') for all x, x' ∈ Euclid P, i.e. G = (fun x => ∫ y, ψ y * g (x - y)) is K-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul). ∎
proof_key_steps: For each x, y ↦ ψ(y)·g(x − y) is continuous with support inside support ψ, hence integrable; ψ and its constant multiples are integrable.
G(x) − G(x') = ∫ (ψ(y)·g(x − y) − ψ(y)·g(x' − y)) dλ(y) by integral_sub.
Pointwise |ψ(y)·g(x − y) − ψ(y)·g(x' − y)| ≤ ψ(y)·K·dist(x, x') since ψ ≥ 0, g is K-Lipschitz and dist(x − y, x' − y) = dist(x, x').
Integrating: |G(x) − G(x')| ≤ K·dist(x, x')·∫ψ dλ = K·dist(x, x'), so G is K-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
